title: Meltemi Weeks: Paros & Naxos on Board and Kite

bestPeriod.window: Mid-June-mid-September for wind; late May and late September for wind plus swimmable calm
bestPeriod.avoid: November-March, most centres shut, ferries cancel on southerlies, and water drops to 15-16°C
bestPeriod.raw: Mid-June-mid-September for wind; late May and late September for wind plus swimmable calm

accommodation.note: Mikri Vigla and Golden Beach studios €80, €140 per night double in August; €55, €90 in June

food.note: Taverna mains €10, €18, beach-club club sandwich €9, half-litre of local white €6

transport.note: Paros-Naxos ferry €13, €35, ATV or small car hire €35, €55/day, airport transfers

activities.note: Six days of kite or windsurf rental €270, €380, one refresher lesson €90, €120, one dive or freedive session €60, €90

profile.difficultyNote: 3/5, no long-distance effort, but six days of 3-5 hours on the water in 20-30 knots is genuinely tiring on shoulders, forearms and neck

gatewayAirport: JTR is wrong for this trip, use PAS Paros National (seasonal Athens and limited European) 20 min to Golden Beach, JNX Naxos Island National 10 min to Naxos Town, or ATH Athens + Blue Star ferry to Paros 3 h 45 min / Naxos 4 h 30 min
summary: This is a week built around a wind that arrives on a timetable. From roughly mid-June the meltemi settles into the Cyclades as a northerly, filling in through the early afternoon and blowing itself out around sunset, and Paros and Naxos sit in the channel where it accelerates hardest. You base first on Paros, Chrisi Akti and New Golden Beach for windsurfing, Pounda for kite in the Antiparos channel, then take the 30-to-45-minute ferry to Naxos, where Mikri Vigla splits into a flat lagoon at Limanaki and a wave side at Orkos in the same ten-minute walk. The rhythm is the same every day: slow mornings, snorkelling and coffee, then a hard three-hour session from about 13:00. It suits an independent intermediate more than a first-timer, because in the second half of July the wind is often too strong for a beginner lesson to even run.

itinerary.title: Land on Paros, rig at New Golden Beach
itinerary.morning: Arrive at Paros (PAS) or off the Blue Star from Piraeus into Parikia. Collect a small car or ATV and drive 20-25 minutes across the island to the Chrisi Akti / New Golden Beach strip on the east coast. Register at Force7 at New Golden Beach: sign the waiver, get sized, and agree the week's rate rather than paying by day.
itinerary.afternoon: Deliberately soft first session. The meltemi is cross-onshore here so a mistake washes you back onto sand, which makes it the right place to shake off a winter. Sail or ride between 13:30 and 16:30, then stop before your forearms decide for you.
itinerary.evening: Taverna Tsachpinis at Drios, five minutes south, for grilled gopa, fava and a carafe of white. Older, cheaper and quieter than the beach-club strip.
itinerary.dayStats: Airport to Golden Beach 20 min / typical afternoon 18-24 knots NNE in June, 22-30 knots in August / water 24-26°C / sail 5.0-5.8 m, kite 8-9 m for 75 kg

itinerary.title: Pounda, the channel and the ferry lane
itinerary.morning: Cross to the west coast to Pounda while the wind is still building. Check in at Paros Kite Pro Center and walk the beach first: the Antiparos ferry lane is the single most important thing on this trip and you need to see where it runs before you are powered up. Rig, then use the light morning breeze for a downwinder-free warm-up.
itinerary.afternoon: Full session at Pounda from about 13:00. Flat sandy shallows close in, chop further out, side-shore meltemi. Set a personal turnaround marker well inside the ferry track and hold it.
itinerary.evening: Drive 25 minutes north to Naoussa. Eat at Siparos on Santa Maria bay if you want the good meal of the week, or at one of the fishing-harbour tavernas in Naoussa itself for grilled octopus and ouzo at half the price.
itinerary.dayStats: Golden Beach to Pounda 25 min / Antiparos ferry crosses every 20-30 min, 07:00-00:30 in summer / Pounda kite day rental €60, €80 / channel Venturi adds roughly 3-6 knots over open-sea forecast

itinerary.title: Kolimbithres, freediving and a windless-morning boat
itinerary.morning: Off the water. Drive to Kolimbithres on the far side of Naoussa Bay, where wind and salt have sculpted the granite into smooth hollows, and snorkel or freedive the rock shelves, 6-12 m of visibility on a calm morning, octopus in the crevices, urchins everywhere, so wear shoes. Aegean Diving College in Naoussa runs guided dives and can put a competent snorkeller onto better ground.
itinerary.afternoon: Either an afternoon session back at New Golden Beach if the meltemi has filled, or the Antiparos option: the ferry from Pounda takes about 10 minutes and lands you in a village that is genuinely quieter than anywhere on Paros.
itinerary.evening: Volcano or Glafkos in Naoussa's old harbour. Order whatever came in that morning, by the kilo.
itinerary.dayStats: Pounda-Antiparos ferry ~10 min, roughly €1.50, €2 foot passenger, €6, €8 with a car / Kolimbithres visibility typically 6-12 m / guided dive €55, €90 / snorkel set hire €10, €15

itinerary.title: Ferry to Naxos, first look at Mikri Vigla
itinerary.morning: Drop the Paros car, take the ferry from Parikia to Naxos Town, Blue Star runs it in about 45 minutes, the fast cats in 25-35. Book the day before in August; the Cycladic ferry network is the trip's one genuine single point of failure. Pick up a car at Naxos port.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive 20 minutes south to Mikri Vigla and walk the headland before you rig. Limanaki on the north side, Orkos on the south, and the granite spine between them, see the difference in water state with your own eyes. Register at Flisvos Kite Centre or Naxos Kitelife. If you want to ride, ride Limanaki.
itinerary.evening: Axiotissa Taverna between Kastraki and Mikri Vigla, vegetable-forward Naxian cooking, its own garden produce, a wine list better than the setting suggests. Book, it fills.
itinerary.dayStats: Parikia-Naxos ferry 25-45 min, roughly €13, €18 conventional, €25, €35 fast / Naxos port to Mikri Vigla 20 min / Limanaki flat-to-chop, Orkos wave and reef

itinerary.title: Limanaki flat water and the Orkos question
itinerary.morning: Coffee at the Flisvos Kite Centre and a slow rig. If you hold an IKO Level 3 card, bring it; without it you will be assessed before you get independent gear. Use the morning for a technique hour, a private lesson here is worth more than three unstructured afternoons.
itinerary.afternoon: Long session on Limanaki. If the meltemi is over 28 knots and clean and you are genuinely a wave rider, cross to Orkos with a partner and a briefed plan; if you are hesitating, that is your answer, and Limanaki will not disappoint you.
itinerary.evening: Kontos Fish Tavern on the Mikri Vigla road, or drive 15 minutes to Plaka for sundown at Kavuras. **Plan B if the wind fails:** swap the afternoon for the Temple of Demeter at Sangri and the Melanes kouros lying unfinished in his orchard.
itinerary.dayStats: Naxos private kite tuition €90, €140/hour / kite day rental €60, €80, six-day €270, €380 / Orkos advanced only, reef and rock section / afternoon peak 14:00-17:00

itinerary.title: Plaka, Laguna and a downwind run
itinerary.morning: Drive the coast road north and look at Plaka's 4 km of open sand and at the Laguna flats behind Agios Prokopios. Laguna is the shallowest, flattest water on the island and the best place on the trip to try a new trick without paying for it.
itinerary.afternoon: Run a supported downwinder, Mikri Vigla to Plaka is the classic, cross-onshore the whole way with sand under you and a road behind the dunes for the pick-up. Arrange the shuttle with your centre in the morning, not at 15:00.
itinerary.evening: Agios Prokopios or Agia Anna for the beach tavernas. Order the Naxian potatoes and the graviera saganaki; this island grows and makes both.
itinerary.dayStats: Mikri Vigla-Plaka downwinder roughly 4-5 km / shuttle €15, €25 pp / Laguna knee-to-waist depth over sand / typical August afternoon 25-32 knots N/NNE

itinerary.title: Agios Georgios, Koufonisia option, Portara at sunset
itinerary.morning: Move to Naxos Town. Agios Georgios is the town beach and a waist-deep lagoon, an easy last wing or windsurf session with Flisvos Sportclub, or the place to put a nervous partner on a board for the first time without any consequence at all.
itinerary.afternoon: If you have a spare day and calm sea, the Small Cyclades day boat to Koufonisia, an hour or so from Naxos, gives you the clearest snorkelling water of the whole trip at Pori and the sea caves along the north shore. Otherwise, wash and return kit and swim off Agios Georgios.
itinerary.evening: Walk the causeway to the Portara, the unfinished 6th-century BC marble doorway of the Temple of Apollo, for sunset, then eat at To Elliniko in the old town.
itinerary.dayStats: Naxos-Koufonisia ferry roughly 55-90 min depending on operator, €18, €30 each way / Agios Georgios sandy and waist-deep 100 m out / Portara free, no fence, no ticket
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Grotta or Nissaki Beach, Naxos Town

accommodationStrategy.name: Golden Beach Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: Directly on the windsurf beach, which removes the single biggest daily friction on a trip like this: you can look at the water from the balcony and decide whether to rig. Rooms are simple, there is outdoor rinse space for kit, and the centres are a two-minute walk. Roughly €90, €150 double in August, €60, €95 in June.

accommodationStrategy.name: Mikri Vigla Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: Sits on the neck of land between Limanaki and Orkos, so both spots are on foot and you can re-check conditions hourly without driving. Kitchenettes matter here because Mikri Vigla has few dinner options and the good tavernas are a drive. Roughly €95, €160 double in season.

accommodationStrategy.name: Nissaki Beach Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: The last-night option: on the Agios Georgios lagoon, walking distance to Flisvos Sportclub, the ferry port and the Portara, which is exactly what you want when you are packing kit and catching a morning boat. Roughly €160, €260 double, and worth it for one night rather than seven.

logistics.connectivity: 4G and increasingly 5G across both islands, weak in the Naxos interior valleys and at Orkos behind the headland. Greece is in the EU so roaming is at domestic rates for EU/EEA SIMs; UK SIMs vary by operator. Download the Windy and Ferryhopper apps and set an offline map before you rely on them at a beach car park.
logistics.emergency: 112 for everything; **Hellenic Coast Guard 108** for anything on the water. Naxos has a general hospital in Naxos Town; Paros has a health centre at Parikia. Serious cases are transferred to Athens by air, which is a real reason to carry insurance that names kitesurfing and windsurfing explicitly, many policies exclude both by default, and freediving below 10 m almost always needs a rider.
logistics.weather: The meltemi is the whole story. It arrives with little visible warning beyond a hard blue sky and a white-capped horizon, it can jump 10 knots in an hour, and it does not respect the "dies at sunset" folklore once it is properly established. Watch the Poseidon System (poseidon.hcmr.gr) alongside Windy, and treat any forecast over 35 knots as a ferry-disruption day as much as a sailing day.
logistics.bookingWindows: August accommodation at Mikri Vigla and Golden Beach goes three to five months out and is the hardest thing to fix late. Ferries: book the Paros-Naxos leg at least 24-48 hours ahead in August, and the Piraeus legs two to four weeks ahead if you are bringing a car. Kite and windsurf week-passes rarely sell out but the good boards do, reserve gear by email a fortnight ahead. Axiotissa needs a day's notice.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are accepted almost everywhere including beach bars, but Greek island card terminals fail with unhelpful regularity, so carry €100, €150 in cash. Tipping is 5-10% or rounding up; it is not obligatory and nobody chases it.
logistics.transportRules: An ATV or quad is the local default but is genuinely dangerous on gravel and, importantly, most travel insurance voids for quad accidents without a category A licence, a small car costs €35, €55 a day and carries a board bag. Taking a hire car between Paros and Naxos on the ferry needs the rental company's written permission and usually costs extra; it is almost always cheaper to hire separately on each island. Ferry tickets must be exchanged for boarding passes at the port for some operators, allow 30 minutes.
logistics.permits: No permit is needed to kite or windsurf, but Greek beach regulation increasingly separates swimmer zones from watersports zones with buoys in high season, respect them, port police do enforce. Anchoring on *Posidonia* seagrass is illegal. Drones need EASA/HCAA registration and are banned over archaeological sites including the Portara and the Temple of Demeter. Spearfishing with scuba is illegal in Greece; removing antiquities from the seabed is a serious criminal matter, and both islands' waters have plenty.
logistics.health: Tap water on Paros is generally not drinkable and on Naxos varies by village, buy or filter. Sea urchins are the number-one injury; carry reef shoes and a needle. Mauve stinger jellyfish come in patches, not blooms, and vinegar is not the recommended treatment for them, hot water immersion is. The meltemi's dry heat masks dehydration badly; two litres per session is a floor, not a target.

proTips: Do your independent-riding paperwork before you leave home. An IKO Level 3 card in your wallet is the difference between renting gear at Mikri Vigla on day one and spending two hours being assessed on day two.

Buy the six-day rental pass at your first centre, not day-by-day. Every centre on both islands discounts hard past four days, and the pass usually includes board storage, which saves you loading a hire car twice a day.
Ride the mornings in July and August. Everyone shows up at 14:00 for the peak; 10:00-12:00 gives you 15-20 knots, an empty beach and a session you can actually repeat the next day.
At Pounda, pick a physical landmark on Antiparos and never go beyond it. The ferry lane is not marked on the water, the ferries are not slow, and the meltemi pushes you toward it.

Take the conventional Blue Star ferry rather than the fast catamaran on any day forecast over 30 knots. The big ships keep sailing when the cats cancel, and a cancelled fast ferry in August rebooks two days later.
Kolimbithres before 09:00. The rock pools are shadeless, the tour boats from Naoussa start at 10:30, and the water is glassiest before the thermal starts.

On Naxos, check both sides of the Mikri Vigla headland every single day. A 3-knot shift or a 20-degree veer turns Limanaki from perfect to unrideable and Orkos from terrifying to sublime, and the walk between them is four minutes.

Eat inland at least twice. Halki, Apeiranthos and Sangri feed you Naxian graviera, kitron and slow-cooked goat for what a beach club charges for a salad, and it is the only way to see that Naxos is a farming island that happens to have beaches.
Book your last night in Naxos Town rather than at the beach. Rinsing salt out of a kite at 22:00 and then driving 20 km to a 06:30 ferry is a bad end to a good week.

raw.Prevailing wind, the meltemi (μελτέμι),: a dry north to north-northeast flow between a Balkan high and an Anatolian low. Season runs May to late September with roughly 70% of episodes falling June-September; July and August are the peak. Typical strength is 4-5 Beaufort (11-21 knots); established episodes commonly run 5-7 Beaufort (17-33 knots) and the strongest August days push 35 knots-plus in the channels. The daily cycle is the thing to plan around: it usually builds from late morning to early afternoon, peaks 14:00-17:00, and softens at sunset, but a properly set-in meltemi does not follow that curve and simply blows for three to ten days without stopping, day and night. In the Paros-Naxos strait, a Venturi between the two islands adds a reliable 3-6 knots over open-sea forecast.
raw.Kit sizing reality: a 75 kg rider in July at Pounda or Mikri Vigla is typically on a 7 m or 8 m kite in the afternoon and a 9 m only in the morning or in September; June and late September more often give 9-12 m. Windsurfers should expect 4.2-5.2 m sails on August afternoons and 5.5-6.5 m in June. Every centre's rental fleet is sized for this, so hiring beats flying kit for a single week.
raw.Launch spots, Paros: *Chrisi Akti (Golden Beach)*, east-facing, coarse sand, cross-onshore in the meltemi, chop building to short 1-1.5 m wind swell by mid-afternoon, intermediate; the historic World Cup windsurf venue on the island. *New Golden Beach (Néa Chrisi Akti)*, immediately north over the headland, the same wind with a longer sandy runway and slightly cleaner water state. *Santa Maria*, north coast, sheltered turquoise bays, sand and seagrass patches, best for SUP, wing and beginner windsurf in lighter morning wind, plus decent snorkelling on the rocky spurs. *Pounda*, west coast facing Antiparos, the island's kite spot, a shallow sandy shelf with side-shore meltemi, flat to light chop, and one serious hazard: the Antiparos car ferry crosses the channel every 20-30 minutes and you must stay out of its lane.
raw.Launch spots, Naxos: *Mikri Vigla* is really two spots either side of a granite headland. *Limanaki*, the north side, is flat-to-choppy, sandy, side-onshore, and the beginner and freestyle side; *Orkos*, the south side, is the wave side with a reef and rock section, more swell, and a stronger, more side-offshore feel, advanced only. *Plaka*, 4 km of west-facing sand between Mikri Vigla and Agios Prokopios, cross-onshore, sandy bottom, big empty runway, the sensible fallback when Mikri Vigla is crowded. *Agios Georgios*, the town beach, is a waist-deep sandy lagoon that stays walkable 100 m out, the safest teaching water in the Cyclades. *Laguna*, behind Agios Prokopios, is a genuinely shallow flat-water lagoon, best in the top half of the tide-free day when the sea breeze is filling.
raw.Equipment hubs and certification: on Naxos, *Flisvos Sportclub* at Agios Georgios (windsurf, wing, SUP, VDWS-affiliated) and its sister *Flisvos Kite Centre* at Mikri Vigla, which teaches to IKO standard and requires an IKO Level 3 card or an on-site competence assessment before it will rent you kite gear independently. *Naxos Kitelife* and *Thalasea Sports* also operate at Mikri Vigla. On Paros, *Paros Kite Pro Center* and *Paros Kite Center* at Pounda, and *Force7 Surf & Kite Center* at New Golden Beach. Indicative 2026 rates: kite equipment day rental €60, €80, six-day pass €270, €380; windsurf funboard rental €25, €50 per hour or €280, €330 per week; a beginner IKO/VDWS kite course of 6-9 hours runs €300, €450 depending on group size, private tuition €90, €140 per hour. Board and rig storage is €5, €10 per day where offered.
raw.Tides and currents, be honest: the Aegean is effectively tideless. Astronomical range at Paros and Naxos is on the order of 0.1-0.3 m, and a strong meltemi's wind set-up moves the waterline more than the moon does. There are no tide windows to plan around. What does matter is wind-driven current: in the Paros-Naxos and Paros-Antiparos channels a sustained northerly pushes a persistent southbound surface drift, so an upwind-limited rider ends up progressively downwind and offshore. Headland acceleration at the Mikri Vigla rock and at Cape Ai Giannis is real and abrupt. Offshore-component danger is concentrated at Orkos and on the north-facing pockets of Santa Maria: if the meltemi backs to NNW, a spot that felt cross-shore becomes cross-offshore and the next land is a long way south.
raw.Sea conditions and safety: water temperature runs roughly 18-19°C in May, 21-22°C in June, 24°C in July, 25-26°C in August, 23-24°C in September and 21-22°C in October. In July and August a shorty or even boardshorts and a lycra is enough for a two-hour session; June and late September justify a 2 mm shorty or 3/2 because 25 knots of dry northerly strips heat fast even off warm water. *Pelagia noctiluca* mauve stingers appear in patchy blooms, worst in late summer and after several calm days, annoying rather than dangerous. Sea urchins are the actual injury statistic here: the rocky ledges at Mikri Vigla's headland, Kolimbithres and Santa Maria's spurs are covered in them, and reef shoes are not optional. Lifeguard coverage on Cycladic beaches is thin and inconsistent even in August; assume there is none. **Hellenic Coast Guard: 108. General emergency: 112.**
raw.Boat and kayak logistics: Greece requires a boat licence for rentals above 30 hp; the standard tourist rental is a 4.7-5.5 m open boat with a 15-30 hp outboard, hireable without a licence for roughly €80, €140 per day plus fuel from Naoussa, Pounda, Aliki and Naxos Town. You sign a declaration and are given a fixed permitted area, typically "no crossing to Naxos" from Paros. Anchoring on *Posidonia oceanica* seagrass is prohibited under Greek law and enforced with fines; anchor on the visible pale sand patches. Small-boat hire is a bad idea on a 30-knot afternoon regardless of licence; do it on a windless morning.
raw.Weather-contingency plan: *No wind*, freedive and snorkel Kolimbithres in Naoussa Bay, dive with an operator out of Naoussa, take the 10-minute Pounda-Antiparos ferry and do the cave, or run the Naxos interior to Apeiranthos and the Melanes kouros. *Too much wind (35 kt+)*, Mikri Vigla's Limanaki side and Naxos's Laguna hold up when Orkos and Golden Beach are unrideable; failing that, this is the day for the Portara at sunset, the Naxos citadel museums, or a Naxian cheese-and-kitron tasting at Halki, and for the fact that Blue Star's big ferries keep running when the fast cats cancel.

sources.confidenceNotes: All rental, lesson and storage prices are indicative and were not confirmed against 2026 published price lists, re-verify with each centre directly. The brief refers to "Pounda's PWA history"; the documented Professional Windsurfers Association World Cup venue on Paros is Chrisi Akti / New Golden Beach on the east coast, with Pounda established later as the kite spot, this file reflects that and the attribution should be double-checked before publishing. Force7 Surf & Kite Center's current operating status at New Golden Beach should be confirmed for 2026. Exact ferry durations and fares for Parikia-Naxos, Pounda-Antiparos and Naxos-Koufonisia vary by operator and season and must be checked live. The Greek unlicensed-boat-rental threshold of 30 hp is the widely applied standard but is administered locally by port authority, confirm with the specific rental. Water-temperature and wind-strength figures are climatological averages, not guarantees. Taverna opening seasons on both islands contract sharply outside June-September.
